name: Databricks
summary: Candidates report a recruiter call, one coding phone screen, then a virtual onsite of about four to five one-hour rounds: algorithm coding, a concurrency or systems programming round, system design, and a behavioural round. Coding is reported as medium to hard, often practical and multi-part with follow-ups.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, interest in Databricks and fit for the role.

rounds.name: Online assessment (some candidates)
rounds.what: CodeSignal test with four questions, usually two medium and two hard.

rounds.name: Technical phone screen
rounds.what: Live coding in CoderPad or similar, LeetCode medium to hard, often with a follow-up part.

rounds.name: Hiring manager call
rounds.what: Mostly behavioural: past work, what you enjoy, team questions. Timing before or after the onsite varies.

rounds.name: Onsite coding (algorithms)
rounds.what: One or two rounds of clean, correct implementation with edge cases, built up in stages.

rounds.name: Onsite concurrency / systems programming
rounds.what: Multithreading and I/O trade-offs, such as a logger or a cached remote file reader.

rounds.name: Onsite system design
rounds.what: Open-ended design expanded from an initial prompt, sometimes done in a shared doc.

rounds.name: Onsite cross-functional / behavioural
rounds.what: Teamwork, conflict and ownership, plus a deep dive on a project you are proud of.

tips: Practise LeetCode questions tagged Databricks from the last few months; reports repeat questions from that pool.
Budget time for edge cases; simple-looking problems lead into follow-ups.
Prepare concurrency basics: locks, queues, buffered writes and disk or network latency trade-offs.
Expect a project deep dive in the behavioural round and know your numbers.
References are reported to carry weight in the final decision.
